title: Scripture and False Teaching
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture and false teaching teaches that God’s Word protects the church from distorted doctrine, deceptive teachers, and messages that turn people away from Christ. False teaching must be tested, rejected, and corrected by Scripture.
summary: Scripture and false teaching teaches that God’s Word protects the church from distorted doctrine, deceptive teachers, and messages that turn people away from Christ. False teaching must be tested, rejected, and corrected by Scripture.
christFocus: False teaching ultimately threatens devotion to Christ by distorting who He is, what He has done, or how sinners are saved. Scripture guards the church by keeping Christ, the Gospel, and sound doctrine at the center.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
False teaching is not a small matter. Scripture warns that distorted doctrine can trouble believers, damage churches, exploit the vulnerable, excuse sin, deny Christ, corrupt the Gospel, and lead people away from the truth.

False teaching often appears attractive. It may use religious language, quote Scripture, promise freedom, flatter listeners, avoid hard truths, or offer a Christ without repentance, a cross without judgment, grace without holiness, or spirituality without obedience.

God’s Word gives the church the standard for testing teaching. The Gospel must not be changed. Christ must not be reduced. Scripture must not be twisted. Teachers must be able to instruct in sound doctrine and correct those who contradict it.

Faithfulness requires both love and courage. The church should not become harsh, suspicious, or quarrelsome, but neither may it tolerate teaching that harms souls. Protecting sound doctrine is an act of love for Christ and His people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
False teaching often harms those who are already weak, wounded, immature, or desperate for hope. People may be drawn in by promises of blessing, healing, secret knowledge, spiritual power, or approval, only to be burdened, deceived, or turned away from the true Gospel.

This doctrine protects the church from replacing Christ with personality, entertainment, greed, legalism, lawlessness, politics, mysticism, or human tradition. God’s people need truth that saves, not messages that merely sound spiritual.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Hold fast to the Gospel and test teaching by Scripture. Do not confuse kindness with silence when truth is being distorted. Refuse to spread teaching that weakens Christ, denies the Gospel, twists Scripture, or excuses sin. Speak correction with humility, courage, and love, aiming to protect souls and honor the Lord.
